result.title: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model
result.summary: Modern video generators excel at producing visually plausible futures guided by text and image prompts. Yet their emphasis on semantic plausibility does not guarantee fidelity to the physical consequences of specific actions. Action-conditioned world models (ACWMs), in contrast, aim to simulate how the world responds to robot actions, enabling scalable policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts. The challenge is not merely to generate a plausible future, but to predict what follows from a specific physical action. As video priors grow stronger, we ask how little adaptation is truly needed to bridge this gap. We introduce Dianjing, a minimal recipe that preserves and unlocks the capabilities of strong video priors through unified physical action conditioning, training concentrated at the high noise levels where motion and layout, and thus the consequences of actions, are decided, and native history conditioning. Built upon MiniMax H3, a 33B video foundation model, Dianjing freezes the pretrained backbone and trains only 0.34% of its parameters using approximately 65 hours of robot video across two embodiments, without additional robot-specific pretraining or camera calibration. Controlled ablations show that where training is allocated across noise levels matters more than how actions enter the network. On WorldOracle, which evaluates predictions against paired real-world executions, Dianjing achieves the best scores on four of the five evaluation tracks and ranks second on AgiBot-Long. Our findings suggest that strong video priors already bring us most of the way to world modeling; lightweight physical action grounding can unlock their potential for real-world prediction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Dianjing，在 33B 视频基础模型上冻结主干、仅训练约 0.34% 参数，用统一动作条件与原生历史条件，将约 65 小时双本体机器人视频适配为动作条件世界模型，并在 WorldOracle 上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「训练集中在高噪声层级」的结论可能与 diffusion 式 latent 推理状态生成中的监督投入与贡献分配问题相关，动作条件未来预测也可类比动作—证据—后果的建模，但跨域可迁移性需核查。
